sentence: This project studies how the expression of DNA is controlled normally and how it goes wrong in neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project builds standardized tools to help diagnose and treat patients with coarctation of the aorta and lower the chance of hypertension.
This project studies how non-growing bacteria survive, to find weak points that antibiotics could target.
This project tests how inherited changes that harm telomere maintenance are linked to age-related disease, with a focus on hematologic disease.
This project runs behavior tests in mice that carry lupus antibodies and records electroencephalogram signals in people doing spatial reasoning activities.
This project uses machine learning and citizen science to study neuropathologic differences of Alzheimer disease within the Hispanic community.
This project builds tissue engineered 3D models of osteosarcoma to learn about its biology, drug resistance and possible therapies.
This project supports research programs and shared resources aimed at reducing the burden of cancer and improving cancer prevention and care.
This project gives biostatistics and bioinformatics support to ovarian research projects, covering data collection, data analysis and data storage.
This project studies how the brain clears waste products, including fluid flow and transport across the blood-brain barrier, in relation to beta-amyloid plaques.
This project supports population science on health differences across groups, reproductive health, migration, and links between genetics or the environment and health.
This project studies how the immune system and cancer interact and works to turn findings in tumor immunology into cancer immunotherapy trials.
This project studies human genetic disorders and inherited disease to learn what causes them and to improve human health.
This project studies the cells, molecules and genes involved in osteonecrosis of the jaw to find genetic risk factors for the condition.
This project studies how asthma contributes to Alzheimer's disease and other dementia using brain imaging, blood biomarkers and a mouse model.
This project studies how lipolytic enzymes are controlled, regulated and inhibited, and how they relate to inflammation and fatty liver disease.
This project maintains a research resource that provides rhesus monkeys for comparative studies in the biomedical and behavioral sciences.
This project builds a cardiac imaging technique called quantitative susceptibility mapping to measure iron in hearts damaged by myocardial infarction.
This project studies the role of the higher order thalamus in cognition and how it interacts with cortex, including in schizophrenia.
This project studies how stem cells in the periodontal crestal region interact with their niche during periodontal tissue regeneration.
